goals.name: ATX Flex Manager + SA Ops Manager Development
goals.assessment: Screening is closed and peer review is in flight across all four branches. Seven of eight applicants qualified (Sullivan Lowe screened out on the six-month Lead bar); no further cut was made at this gate — the cover-letter instruction shipped in the messaging but never made it onto the application link, so a weak application score can't be cleanly read as low effort versus a missed instruction. Scoring model rebuilt to weight only evidence-carrying categories: On-Site Evaluations 30, Peer Review 30, Application 25, EMC Games 15, with résumé/tenure/attempts as reference. Games no longer scales down — 10+ on the 1–13 scale is the top score. Application grade now measures the whole written case wherever the candidate made it, with a missing cover letter recorded as a miss but unweighted. Peer evaluation forms built and sent per branch, each naming the South Austin position explicitly; South Austin and Houston ride Training Days 8/19 and 8/20, North Austin is pulsed to Daniel Behseresht with an 80%-response target, Fort Worth sent direct with Mike in the loop. Rationale posted to the live pulse for Cameron and Anne. Projects added as a distinct stage between peer review and interviews. Seats already closed: Daniel Behseresht N. Austin BM (8/10), Hector Zavala S. Austin Ops (8/11), Calvin Hughes to Remote Flex (8/11). Peer score averages are being pulled 8/24 and land on the applicant scorecard by EOD, which produces the advance/hold decision for the projects stage. Immediately after: define the projects themselves, assign dates, and close the loop directly with the candidates not moving forward — that conversation is part of the rock, not an afterthought, since six of seven applicants are current employees who stay on the team either way. Remaining after that: the project stage, interviews, the decision, and the documented 30/60/90 the green bar actually requires.

goals.name: CTXH Quarterly Theme Mgmt — Ensure All Managers Hit QGs
goals.assessment: Both hard deadlines were met. Manager sandbox training finished 15 of 15 — Daniel B., Nick D., Jespah L. and Joel V. closed out on the 8/19 deadline, and Sergio Buenrostro completed 8/24 on his documented extended timeline (approved PTO predating the deadline). 100% of active movers were enrolled in the training app on 8/20 as planned. That clears two of the three green conditions. The whole rock now rests on the third: the adoption floor of ≥70% of enrolled movers through stage 4 by EOQ. That is a 10-week behavior problem, not a deadline problem, and it has not started — which is why confidence stays at 4 rather than rising with the percentage. Note the rock is training-camp completion and adoption, not general QG accountability.

goals.name: Scrum Accountability Part 3 — Huddle Grading + Value Tracking
goals.assessment: Infrastructure is complete and corrected; distribution is still the one gate. The 8/21 invite date was missed for a real reason — the manager instructions came back with discrepancies that had to be fixed before anything went out, and that fix landed Friday 8/21 ahead of Brian being out of office. Invites and the announcement push today, 8/24. Also corrected: the rollout announcement claimed a 14-criterion / 70-point mock rubric that never existed — real rubric is 12 criteria / 60 points on both mock and live boards, and all 5 branch boards already carried the Owner and Definition-of-Done columns, so the 8/14 change closed a parity gap rather than opening one. Mock-board baseline corrected from 29/70 (41%) to 29/60 (48%, F) in the scorecard tool, the HQ, and memory. Scrum HQ republished 8/24. Per Brian's 8/24 call, individual grading and certification results stay private rather than published. Still standing: mock board trimmed to 32 pulses and duplicated for all 15 managers, Board Fix-It Checklist published, dashboard Certifications section built and ready to log.
